item.title: Reps fault removal of civic education, computer studies from WAEC portal
item.description: The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Government, through the Ministry of Education, to rethink the removal of Civic Education, Computer Studies, and Electrical Installation, among others, from the West African Examination Council portal, citing the significance of the subjects to national development.The resolution of the House followed the consideration and adoption of a motion of urgent public importance moved during Thursday’s plenary by the member representing Yenagoa/Opokuma F

item.title: Kogi LG imposes curfew, bans vigils over rising insecurity
item.description: The Chairman of Omala Local Government Area of Kogi State, Edibo Mark, has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew amid escalating security concerns in the council area.The curfew, which runs from 7 pm to 6 am daily, took effect on December 2 and will remain in force until further notice.The council also announced 24-hour security surveillance and intensified patrols across all communities.In a statement on Thursday, Mark said the measure became necessary to protect lives and property following recent sec

item.title: FG Begins Direct Stipend Payments to 42,000 TVET Trainees Nationwide
item.description: The Federal Government has kicked off the disbursement of the first tranche of funds under its renewed Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programme, directly crediting over 42,000 students and more than 600 accredited training centres across Nigeria.Each of the 42,000 beneficiaries now receives a monthly stipend of ₦22,500 to cover living and transport expenses, allowing them to focus entirely on their vocational training without financial distraction.At the same time, over 6

item.title: Sokoto Police Arrest Three Key Financiers of Lakurawa Bandits
item.description: Sokoto State Police Command has apprehended three suspected financiers and informants linked to the notorious Lakurawa bandit group, among them Ruwa Ginyo, the recognised Fulani head (Sarkin Fulani) of Gidan-Madi community in Tangaza Local Government Area.The trio were arrested on Tuesday, 3 December 2025, around 2:00 p.m. while allegedly trying to sell four rustled cows to innocent buyers in a local market.Preliminary investigation showed that the suspects specialise in disposing of cattle stol

item.title: Gov. Buni Approves Scholarships for 28,346 Yobe Students, Doubles All Allowances
item.description: Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, has approved full scholarship payments for a historic 28,346 indigenous students studying in universities, polytechnics, colleges of education and other tertiary institutions across Nigeria.In a landmark move, the governor also approved a 100% increase in all scholarship categories, effectively doubling the monthly allowances students receive to cushion the impact of rising living and educational costs.Breakdown of the new doubled allowances:PhD, Master’s and

item.title: Police warn against fireworks, knockouts ahead of Christmas in Delta
item.description: As part of measures to ensure a safe and peaceful Yuletide season, the Delta State Police Command has reiterated that the ban on fireworks remains in force and will be strictly enforced.The ban, according to the state Commissioner of Police, Olufemi Abaniwonda, covers “The use, sale, and display of pyrotechnics, including fireworks and firecrackers known as ‘knockouts’ and ‘bangers’.”This was contained in a statement signed by the state Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe, and made

item.title: Zamfara proposes N861bn budget for 2026 fiscal year
item.description: The Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has proposed a budget of N861bn for the 2026 fiscal year.Presenting the appropriation bill before the state House of Assembly on Thursday, the governor said N715bn was earmarked for capital expenditure, representing 83 per cent of the budget.Lawal added that N147.2bn, representing 17 per cent, was allocated for recurrent expenditure.The health sector received the highest allocation of N87bn, followed by agriculture, which also got N87bn.The education sect

item.title: Troops Arrest Seven Suspected Bandits Along Benin-Agbor Highway

item.title: Why Football Remains Nigeria’s Betting King: And What That Means for Leagues
item.description: Football is more than a sport in Nigeria. It is part of daily life. People shout about matches in markets, on buses, and in group chats. Old men argue about players.
